audit_result.code_path: supabase/migrations/0000_create_member_schema.sql::CREATE POLICY Allow user to update their own profile::L83
audit_result.proof_trace: The RLS UPDATE policy `USING (auth.uid() = id)` has no `WITH CHECK` clause restricting updatable columns, and the default privilege `grant all on tables to authenticated` grants UPDATE on every column including `is_admin`. No trigger or column-level grant blocks `is_admin` writes. The `20260317000001_fix_security_permissions.sql` security fix applied FORCE RLS and revoked anon access but left this policy intact, so the column-level gap persists.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An authenticated attacker sends `PATCH /rest/v1/member.members?id=eq.<attacker-uuid>` with body `{"is_admin": true}` using their own Supabase JWT; the RLS policy permits the update because `auth.uid() = id` is satisfied and no column restriction exists, escalating the attacker to admin.

PROP-kintai-v3-st-inv-003.text: Users must not be able to UPDATE their own role field via RLS-permitted self-update.
PROP-kintai-v3-st-inv-003.assertion: forall u: update_user(u, fields) => 'role' NOT IN fields OR is_admin(u) == true
